newsitem.title: DENMARK: Higher Q3 sales, product mix boost Novo.
newsitem.headline: Higher Q3 sales, product mix boost Novo.

text.p: Danish drugs and biotechnology group Novo Nordisk reported on Wednesday better than expected profits for 1996's first nine months, helped along by palpable advances in sales and an improved product mix in its key health care and enzyme operations.

Novo Nordisk, one of the world's leading producers of insulin and industrial enzyme products, upheld its six month-old forecast of whole year 1996 operating and pre-tax profits 10-15 percent better than 1995, when the group posted a 2.156 billion crown pre-tax and extraordinary items profit.

"Economic factors that could cause results to differ include unexpected developments in the international and securities markets or tax rate changes, price decreases in major markets including Japan, the United States and Europe and competing products within the company's key business areas," Novo said in a statement.
Novo posted a 1.893 billion crown pre-tax profit for 1996's first nine months, 14 percent up on the same period last year and better than analysts' average expectations of 1.852 billion crowns.
Operating income increased 12 percent in the period to 1.893 billion crowns on four percent higher consolidated sales of 10.725 billion crowns.

Novo's Health Care unit, which makes insulin, human growth hormone and gynaecological products, posted an eight percent sales increase to 7.931 billion crowns over the same period last year, with sales of diabetes care products 12 percent up.
This reflected in particular higher sales of disposable insulin pen dispensers notably in Japan and the United States, Novo said.
It said increased competition in Britain meant sales of women's hormone replacement therapy products only rose two percent globally in the year's first nine months.
Novo said though sales of its anti-depressant Seroxat pill in the Nordic region were up 30 percent, with new products for haemophiliacs and epileptics doing well.
Novo's Enzyme unit, which makes industrial enzymes for the detergent, textile, starch, baking, animal feed and brewing industries, reported seven percent higher sales at 2.575 billion crowns.
